info.title: B2B Expense & Team Budget Tracker
info.summary: Expense claims, department budgets and recurring vendor spend for multi-tenant B2B customers.
info.description:
Tenancy is enforced by PostgreSQL row-level security, not by application filters. The tenant travels only in the signed access token: there is no tenant header, path segment or query parameter, because any of those would be a value the client chooses.

Money is always an integer count of minor units plus a currency. No amount is ever a JSON number with a decimal point: JSON numbers are IEEE 754 doubles in every browser, and a system that sums thousands of expense lines that way produces totals that disagree with the receipts.

Errors share one envelope. The status code is chosen for what the client should do next: 401 log in, 402 change plan, 403 ask someone else, 404 stop asking, 409 reload and retry, 413 narrow the range, 422 fix a field, 503 retry later.

post.description: Returns an access token in the body and a refresh token in an HttpOnly cookie. The refresh token is deliberately not repeated in the body: that is the difference between an XSS bug costing fifteen minutes and costing thirty days.
Takes no access token on purpose: a session whose access token has already expired must still be endable, or a client is left holding a live refresh token it cannot revoke. Clears the refresh cookie.

Each refresh token may be exchanged once. A token that comes back after use is evidence of theft, so the whole rotation family is revoked - both the thief's session and the victim's, because there is no way to tell which is which.

post.summary: Register a user and their first organisation
post.description: Signing up is signing up an organisation: a user with no membership can authenticate and then do nothing, because every endpoint resolves an actor first.

post.summary: Issue a token for another organisation
post.description: A new token rather than an amended one: the tenant claim is what the database session is bound to, so it has to be signed.

get.description: Counts approved and paid claims only. Counting pending ones would let anybody exhaust a budget on paper.
Readable by any active member: filing a claim requires picking one.

delete.description: Archives rather than deletes. The foreign keys are ON DELETE RESTRICT, and archiving keeps historical claims attributable.

get.description: Keyset pagination. OFFSET makes the last page the most expensive and shifts the window when rows are inserted mid-walk; a cursor over (spent_at, id) costs the same at page one and page one thousand.
Oldest first, which is the opposite of every other listing: a queue is worked from the front. Served from a partial index holding only pending rows.
Includes allowed_actions, so the dashboard renders buttons that work without reimplementing the state machine.

get.summary: The append-only audit ledger for a claim

post.description: Requires a payment reference, and refuses the approver of the same claim - an owner holds both permissions, so a role check alone would not stop them.
Requires a reason. Also bounded by the approval ceiling: a manager who cannot approve a large claim should not be able to dispose of it either, because that closes the escalation path.

post.summary: Reopen a rejected claim as the next draft revision
post.description: The only way forward from rejected. There is no rejected to pending_approval edge: without the revision step a submitter could re-present an identical claim until an approver clicked the wrong button.

post.summary: Pull a pending claim back to draft
post.description: Does not start a new revision: nobody decided anything.
You may only invite somebody below your own role.

patch.summary: Change a member's role, status, department or approval limit
patch.description: You may not change your own standing, in either direction: self-demotion by an owner leaves an organisation nobody can administer.

get.summary: Stream an expense report as CSV, XLSX or PDF
get.description: Nothing is buffered: the response is chunked and produced as the rows are read. A failure after the first byte cannot be a status code, so it becomes a deliberately aborted connection - a truncated download rather than a complete-looking file missing half the year.

413.description: The range exceeds the synchronous row limit for this plan.

get.summary: Totals by status and by department
get.description: Computed in SQL. A dashboard summing its first page reports the wrong total for any tenant with more than one page, and is wrong in a way that looks plausible.
The customer's own recurring software spend, with an annualised total.

patch.summary: Update or cancel a tracked subscription

post.summary: Receive a subscription event from the payment gateway
post.description: Authenticated by HMAC, not by a bearer token. The signature is verified before the event id is claimed: claiming first would let anyone POST a guessed id, plant a settled row, and have the genuine delivery discarded as a duplicate.

parameters.name: X-Billing-Signature
parameters.description: t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex hmac-sha256> over "<timestamp>." + the raw body. Several v1 values may appear during a secret rotation.

400.description: The signature does not verify. The gateway must not redeliver: it never will.

408.description: The delivery is outside the tolerance window. Worth redelivering if the clocks are what is wrong.

get.description: Touches nothing. A liveness probe that checks a dependency restarts the process when the dependency fails, turning a database blip into a rolling restart of every replica.
Checks the database, because a replica that cannot reach it can serve nothing.

bearerAuth.description: A short-lived access token carrying the user and the tenant. The role is deliberately not in the token: a token issued before a demotion would otherwise keep its old authority until it expired.

relaySignature.name: X-Billing-Signature
relaySignature.description: HMAC-SHA256 over the timestamp and the raw body, verified before the event id is claimed.

Cursor.name: cursor
Cursor.description: Opaque keyset cursor from a previous page's next_cursor. Not a page number: the position is (spent_at, id), so inserts during a walk cannot shift the window.

FilterFrom.name: from
FilterFrom.description: Inclusive lower bound on spent_at - the date on the receipt, not the date the claim was filed.

FilterSearch.name: q
FilterSearch.description: Substring match on merchant and description, served by a trigram index.

Money.description: An exact amount in the minor units of a currency. Never a decimal number: see the API description.

formatted.description: Rendered with the currency's own exponent - two places for USD, none for JPY, three for KWD.

submitter_id.description: A membership id, not a user id: the same person in two organisations is two submitters.

spent_at.description: The date on the receipt. Reporting periods key on this, not on when the claim was filed.

revision.description: Increments when a rejected claim is revised, so an approver can tell revision 2 from the one they already refused.

version.description: Optimistic concurrency token. Two approvers deciding at once produce one decision and one 409.

allowed_actions.description: Exactly the actions this caller may take right now. Asserted by test to match what the transition endpoints accept, so a rendered button never 403s.

has_more.description: Exact, without a COUNT: the query fetches one row beyond the page.

message.description: Withheld for 5xx: an internal failure's text can name a table, a constraint or a host.

trace_id.description: Matches X-Request-Id, and appears on every log line for the request.

Unauthorized.description: No valid credential. Every rejected token gets the same answer: distinguishing expired from malformed from wrongly-signed tells a forger which part to fix next.

Forbidden.description: Authenticated, but not permitted. Ask someone else - this will not resolve by retrying.

NotFound.description: No such resource, or none you may see. The two are deliberately indistinguishable: a 403 on a resource outside your scope would confirm the id exists.

Conflict.description: The request was well formed and the world moved - a lost compare-and-swap, or a state that no longer permits the action. Reload and decide again.

Invalid.description: Well formed, but the values are wrong. The fields array names each one.

PlanLimit.description: The organisation is at its plan's ceiling for this resource. Not a 403: the caller has the authority, and an administrator cannot help - the fix is a plan change.

RateLimited.description: Too many requests. The limiter is in-process and therefore per replica - a deliberate trade: a shared limiter in Redis is exact but puts a network round trip and a failure mode in front of the credential endpoints. Retry-After says when to come back.
